intro: Four modules follow the DP-900 skills measured: core data concepts, relational data, non-relational data and analytics workloads.

sources.title: Microsoft Learn: Study guide for Exam DP-900

modules.title: Describe core data concepts
modules.summary: Structured, semi-structured and unstructured data, file formats, data roles, and transactional versus analytical workloads.

guide.html: Structured data fits tables with a fixed schema (a SQL table). Semi-structured data has tags or keys but a flexible shape (JSON, XML). Unstructured data has no model (images, video, documents). Common file formats: CSV, JSON, XML, Parquet (columnar, compressed, good for analytics) and Avro.

OLTP (transactional) handles many small reads and writes with ACID guarantees. OLAP (analytical) handles large aggregations across history. Batch processing runs on collected data; streaming processes events as they arrive. Roles: database administrator (manages and secures databases), data engineer (builds pipelines), data analyst (builds reports and models).
Atomicity (all or nothing), Consistency (valid state), Isolation (concurrent transactions do not interfere) and Durability (committed data survives failure).

tips: Parquet is columnar, ideal for analytics.
terms: Data with a fixed schema in rows and columns.
Self-describing data with flexible structure, such as JSON.
A columnar file format for analytics.

modules.title: Describe relational data on Azure
modules.summary: Relational concepts, SQL, and Azure SQL and open-source database options.

guide.html: Tables have rows and columns; a primary key uniquely identifies a row and a foreign key links tables. Normalization reduces duplication. Views store queries, indexes speed lookups, stored procedures package logic. SQL groups: DDL (CREATE, ALTER, DROP), DML (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, SELECT) and DCL (GRANT, REVOKE).

Azure SQL Database is a PaaS single database or elastic pool. Azure SQL Managed Instance gives near-full SQL Server compatibility as PaaS. SQL Server on Azure VMs is IaaS with full control. Open-source engines are offered as managed services: Azure Database for PostgreSQL and MySQL.

tips: Managed Instance = easiest migration with high compatibility.
SQL on a VM = most control, most administration.
terms: Column that uniquely identifies each row.
Column referencing a primary key in another table.

modules.title: Describe non-relational data on Azure
modules.summary: Blob, Data Lake, Files, Table storage, and Azure Cosmos DB APIs.

guide.html: Blob storage holds unstructured objects; with a hierarchical namespace it becomes Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 for analytics. Azure Files provides SMB/NFS file shares. Table storage is a simple key-value store. Blob access tiers: hot, cool, cold, archive.

Azure Cosmos DB is a globally distributed, multi-model NoSQL database with low latency and elastic scale. APIs: NoSQL (documents), MongoDB, Cassandra (wide-column), Gremlin (graph) and Table. NoSQL types: key-value, document, column-family and graph.

tips: Hierarchical namespace turns Blob into Data Lake Storage.
terms: Blob with hierarchical namespace for analytics.
Managed file shares over SMB or NFS.

modules.title: Describe an analytics workload on Azure
modules.summary: Data warehousing, ingestion, Microsoft Fabric, Synapse, Databricks, streaming, and Power BI.

guide.html: Typical flow: ingest data, store it (data lake or warehouse), process it (ETL or ELT), then visualize. A data warehouse holds structured, modeled data in a star schema with fact tables (measurements) and dimension tables (descriptions). A data lakehouse combines lake flexibility with warehouse features.

Microsoft Fabric is the unified SaaS analytics platform (OneLake, Data Factory, Real-Time Intelligence, Power BI). Azure Synapse Analytics offers pipelines, SQL and Spark. Azure Databricks is an Apache Spark based platform. Azure Data Factory orchestrates data movement. Azure Stream Analytics and Event Hubs handle streaming data.
Parts: Power BI Desktop (author), the Power BI service (share) and mobile apps. Building blocks: dataset/semantic model, report (multiple pages) and dashboard (pinned tiles from reports).

tips: Fact tables hold numbers; dimension tables describe them.
ETL transforms before loading; ELT loads then transforms.
A dashboard is a single page of pinned tiles.
